gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Apple lists only its 140 W adapter for fast-charging a 16-inch MacBook Pro, and no 96 W or 100 W option. Also missing: 16-inch M1/M2 models can take 140 W only over a USB-C-to-MagSafe 3 cable, while Nov 2023 (M3) and later models can also take it over USB-C with a 240 W EPR cable. A 100 W charger or 100 W (5 A) cable, ChatGPT's 'default recommendation' for 'MacBook Pro', is not on Apple's fast-charge list for the 16-inch.
standout_why: I compared against the four anker.com pages in ChatGPT's results: A2688 Prime 100W, A120F Laptop Charger Pro, A121B 100W Smart Display and the 'Chargers For Laptop' collection. A2688 says only 'For optimal 100W charging, use an E-Marker cable' and lists 'MacBook Air / Pro Series' without naming the 16-inch. A120F claims fast charging only for the 14-inch MacBook Pro (M5). A121B lists 'MacBook Air/Pro' with no cable or model limits. The collection page says it gives no wattage per laptop and lists no exclusions. None of them states the 16-inch's 140 W requirement, the M1/M2 MagSafe-only rule or the 240 W EPR cable needed above 100 W. ChatGPT's own table puts 'MacBook Pro' under 100 W.
decides: This splits the pick by laptop. On Apple's list, a 100 W charger (Anker Prime 100W, UGREEN Nexode 100W) can fast-charge a 14-inch MacBook Pro (Apple lists 96 W) and a MacBook Air (Apple lists 70 W or more, or 67 W for 13.6-inch only), but not a 16-inch MacBook Pro. A 16-inch owner needs a 140 W PD 3.1 charger such as the Anker Prime 160W A2687 or AOHi The Youth 140W, plus the right cable: USB-C to MagSafe 3 for M1/M2, or MagSafe 3 or a 240 W EPR USB-C cable for M3 and later. A 5 A, 100 W cable caps output at 100 W. AOHi's two USB-C ports drop to 65 W each when a second device is plugged in (Notebookcheck), so it gives 140 W only to a laptop charging alone. The page should add a 'which MacBook / which cable' row.

findings.label: Adapters and cables Apple lists for fast charging (to 50% in about 30 min)
findings.value: Two options: the 140 W USB-C Power Adapter with a USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable, or the 140 W adapter with the 240 W USB-C Charge Cable on MacBook Pro (16-inch, Nov 2023) or later. The Apple Studio Display XDR is also listed. No 96 W or 70 W adapter is listed for the 16-inch.
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: The page's published date is 2026-11-05. It names only Apple adapters and cables and does not mention third-party adapters.

findings.label: Adapters Apple lists for fast charging
findings.value: 140 W or 96 W USB-C Power Adapter, with a USB-C to MagSafe 3 or USB-C charge cable. A third-party display qualifies only if rated for 94 W.
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: Applies to 14-inch models from 2021 on. The 94 W display threshold is the only third-party wattage Apple gives for this model.

findings.label: Adapters Apple lists for fast charging
findings.value: 140 W, 96 W or 70 W USB-C Power Adapter. The 67 W adapter is listed for 13.6-inch models only. A third-party display qualifies if rated for 85 W.
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: The 15-inch Air is not on the 67 W line, so Apple's lowest listed adapter for it is 70 W.

findings.label: Cable needed for 140 W on a 16-inch MacBook Pro, by chip
findings.value: M1 and M2: USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable only. M3 and M4: an EPR (140 W/240 W) USB-C to USB-C cable or a USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable. Power drops automatically once the battery passes 80%.
findings.source_title: Why can't the single-port output of Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) reach 140W? - Anker Support
findings.note: Maker FAQ. Consistent with Apple's 'Nov 2023 or later' rule for the 240 W USB-C cable, since Nov 2023 is the M3 generation.

findings.label: Cable power tiers the charger's display reports
findings.value: 3A cable up to 60 W, 5A cable up to 100 W, EPR cable up to 240 W
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) - Anker US
findings.note: Maker's statement of what each cable class carries. A non-EPR 5 A cable stops at 100 W, so it cannot carry the 140 W (28 V) profile.

findings.label: Single-port output profiles and US-voltage derating
findings.value: 5V⎓3A / 9V⎓3A / 15V⎓3A / 20V⎓5A / 28V⎓5A / 28V⎓5.36A, labelled '150W Max'; the Key Features section says '140W Single-Port Output'. Footnote: single-port charging runs without derating at 77°F in 220–240 V areas, and in 100–130 V areas for at least 1 hour.
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) - Anker US
findings.note: The page does not reconcile 140 W and 150 W; the FAQ says 150 W applies only to some Anker devices in AI Mode 2.0. Total output is 160 W with two or three ports in use, and the page gives no fixed per-port split.

findings.label: Price, Anker US store
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) - Anker US
findings.note: Read through a page fetch. The 'Chargers For Laptop' collection page showed $115.99 (regularly $149.99) on the same day, so the sale price varies by page or variant.

findings.label: Voltage and cable needed above 100 W
findings.value: USB PD was limited to 100 W at 20 V with USB Type-C cables rated at 5 A. The new 28 V, 36 V and 48 V fixed voltages enable 140 W, 180 W and 240 W. USB Type-C spec Release 2.1 defines the 240 W cable requirements.
findings.note: This is why a '100W' cable cannot deliver 140 W even from a 140 W charger.

findings.label: Maker's port, cable and exclusion notes
findings.value: Use USB-C1 (top port) for the laptop when both USB-C ports are in use. Total is 100 W with two ports and 89 W with three. 'For optimal 100W charging, use an E-Marker cable.' Apple's 5.9-ft Thunderbolt cable is not compatible with certain Samsung, Dell and Lenovo models. Cables are sold separately. Listed as Sold Out on Anker US.
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (100W, 3 Ports, GaN) - Anker US
findings.note: This is a cited rival page; the e-marker note is already public there. The page shows no price because the product is sold out.

findings.label: Two-port split
findings.value: C1 + C2: 70 W + 30 W (or 95 W + 5 W with a low-current device). C + A: 67 W + 33 W. All three ports: 80 W + 12 W + 7.5 W. Sold Out.
findings.source_title: Anker Charger (100W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) - Anker US
findings.note: Rival page. A laptop gets 70 W, not 100 W, while a phone shares the USB-C ports.

findings.label: Device limits
findings.value: Single USB-C port, charges one device at a time. Anker's internal test: 14-inch MacBook Pro (M5) 0–50% in 30 min. Recognizing Windows laptops (ThinkPad X1, Dell XPS) requires the Anker Charging Manager app. Connected to a hub's PD port, it charges but cannot connect to the app. Price $59.99 on the product page; $49.99 on the collection page the same day.
findings.source_title: Anker 100W USB-C GaN Charger (Battery Care and Smart Display) - Anker US
findings.note: Rival page. Its fast-charge claim covers only the 14-inch MacBook Pro.

findings.label: Output with two devices plugged in
findings.value: 140 W on one USB-C port (PD 3.1); 65 W each when two devices charge at once. Introductory price $69.99.

A maker statement that the 16-inch MacBook Pro M1/M2 USB-C (Thunderbolt) ports cap at 100 W. Apple's page shows it only by omission, and Anker's FAQ says 'M1/M2: MagSafe 3 only'. I did not find an Apple tech-spec line giving the USB-C port's wattage.
